A feature release, not a patch — several things landed since 0.1.1-beta, on
top of `main` and `develop` finally being reconciled after diverging for a
few weeks (see below if you're curious why that happened).

Still a beta. The Windows installer's wizard, the WSL integration, and the
new Settings UI sections it added have not yet been through a human's hands
on a real machine — only automated checks.

## New: pick your own orb colours

Slate, violet and amber were never meant to be the only option — see
**Orb colours** in the Settings window to change the idle / working / needs-you
colours the orb and the menu-bar icon both use. Leave a colour alone and it
keeps following the built-in default, so a future retune of the shipped
palette still reaches you. **Reset** puts all three back.

## New: control how long a quiet orb sticks around

**Keep orbs for**, also in Settings — 1 minute up to 4 hours, or **Forever**.
A session waiting on you is never pruned early no matter what this is set to;
it only affects orbs that have gone quiet on their own.

## New: agent teams get drawn as teams

A team of Claude Code agents used to show up as unrelated-looking orbs, one
per process, all sharing the team session's title. Now each member is drawn
smaller with a tapered arrow pointing at the lead's orb, lettered and labelled
with **the agent's own name** instead. Dragging a lead moves its whole team;
dragging a member pulls just that one out. No hook changes needed — Claude
Code already hands over `--parent-session-id`, `--agent-name` and
`--agent-color` on the command line for each member process.

## New: drag an orb, and it stays put

Left-click-drag an orb to reposition it, and it holds that spot across
restarts — keyed by working directory, so it survives session ids changing
between runs. Right-click → **"Return this orb to the stack"** gives the
placement up.

## New: a Mac-native Settings window

Rebuilt to match System Settings' own shape — grouped cards, hairline
dividers, the system's real translucency instead of an approximation, and a
working switch control instead of a checkbox standing in for one.

## New (Windows): WSL integration and multiple Claude Code accounts

Originally shipped straight to `main` (see below) — Claude Buddy can now
track a Claude Code session running inside a WSL distro, not just a native
Windows one, and the Settings window gained a checkbox per distro to wire or
unwire it. Separately, **CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR** accounts (e.g.
`alias kwork="CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-work claude"` for a second account)
can now be added in Settings so Claude Buddy's hooks reach them too, on both
native Windows and every wired WSL distro.

**Not yet verified on a real machine.** Automated CI covers native
install/uninstall and hook wiring, but nobody has clicked through the new WSL
checkbox, the Claude Code profiles section, or watched a WSL session's orb
actually appear — see `docs/windows-wsl-integration-verify.md` for the
outstanding manual pass.

## Fixed: settings could silently fail to save on a real Windows install

A trimmed, self-contained publish (the actual shipped Windows build) hit a
missing `TypeInfoResolver` on every write to `settings.json`, and swallowed
the exception — so a preference change looked like it took, and then wasn't
there next launch, with nothing in the UI ever admitting a problem. Fixed,
and failures now leave a breadcrumb in
`%TEMP%\claude_buddy\settings-errors.log` (or the macOS equivalent) instead of
disappearing.

## Why `main` and `develop` needed reconciling

The WSL/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR work above was opened against `main` directly
instead of `develop`, per this repo's own branching rules. The two branches
then diverged for about three weeks — `main` had the WSL commits `develop`
lacked, `develop` had everything above that `main` lacked — until this release
branch merged `main`'s WSL work back into `develop` first, so this release
carries both in full rather than only one side of it.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `ClaudeBuddy-0.2.0-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `ClaudeBuddy-0.2.0-beta-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `ClaudeBuddy-0.2.0-beta-win-x64-setup.exe` |

The .NET runtime is bundled; nothing else is needed. `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers every
file — verify with `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` on macOS or
`Get-FileHash <file> -Algorithm SHA256` on Windows.

## Upgrading from 0.1.1-beta

**macOS**: replace the app in Applications. The signing identity is unchanged, so
your Automation permission carries over and click-to-focus keeps working. Hooks are
already wired; you don't need to run the hook installer again.

**Windows**: run the new setup over the old one. It upgrades in place, closing a
running copy if needed, and leaves your hook configuration alone.

## Installing fresh

**macOS** — open the DMG, drag Claude Buddy to Applications, then double-click
**Install Claude Code Hooks.command**. Launch from Applications; nothing appears in
the Dock and no window opens, which is correct — look in the menu bar.

**Windows** — run the setup. Per-user, so no UAC prompt. Leave both checkboxes
ticked; tick **"Wire hooks for Claude Code running inside WSL"** too if you use it.

### The hook step is not optional

Claude Buddy learns about your sessions from a hook Claude Code runs. Until it is
in `~/.claude/settings.json`, the app starts and runs correctly and shows **nothing
at all**. The installers offer to wire it up; let them. Existing settings are backed
up first, and re-running repairs rather than duplicating.

Hooks are read once at session start, so **restart any open Claude Code sessions**.

## Known limitations

- **Windows installers are unsigned** — SmartScreen warns; choose **More info → Run
  anyway**. The macOS builds are signed and notarized, so they open normally.
- **The Windows wizard, WSL integration, and the new Settings UI sections have
  only been verified automatically**, not by a person on a real machine — see
  above.
- **WSL + tmux together isn't covered.**
- A session killed with Ctrl+C at a permission prompt can leave its orb stuck on
  amber. Right-click → *Reset this session to idle* clears it.
